planted.summary: Cron endpoint is open to anyone when CRON_SECRET is unset.
OAuth state check is skipped when the state cookie is missing, so a forged callback links an attacker's Whoop account.
deleteSubscription ignores userId, so any signed-in user can delete another user's push subscription by endpoint.
repeatMeal reads the source meal by id only, so a user can copy any other user's meal into their own log.
settingsSchema passes unknown keys through and the result is spread into the update, so a client can overwrite any profiles column, user_id included.
A server action returns the decrypted provider API key to the browser.
Coach replies are model output rendered with rehype-raw, so HTML in a reply (or injected into one) executes in the page.
The next query parameter is used as a redirect target, and an absolute URL sends the user to any external site.

findings.title: Cron endpoint fails open when CRON_SECRET is unset
findings.evidence: `if (cronSecret && auth !== `Bearer ${cronSecret}`) { ...401 }` — the authorization check is skipped entirely when the env var is missing, so any unauthenticated attacker can GET /api/cron/maintenance and force expireStaleFacts/consolidateMemories/pruneEvents to run (data deletion plus AI cost).

findings.title: Unvalidated `next` query param used as redirect target
findings.evidence: `return NextResponse.redirect(new URL(next ?? "/settings?whoop=env", request.url));` — a logged-in user clicking /api/whoop/connect?next=https://evil.example is redirected off-site (the `new URL` constructor honors absolute attacker URLs), enabling credential-phishing redirects from a trusted origin.

findings.title: OAuth state check skipped when the state cookie is absent
findings.evidence: `if (!code || (expected && state !== expected))` — if `whoop_oauth_state` is not present on the request (e.g. the victim is sent straight to /api/whoop/callback without visiting /connect), `expected` is undefined and the comparison is bypassed, letting an attacker complete the flow with their own WHOOP account and bind it to the victim's account.

findings.title: deleteSubscription ignores userId and deletes any user's subscription
findings.evidence: `.where(eq(push_subscriptions.endpoint, endpoint))` drops the ownership filter even though `userId` is a parameter, so DELETE /api/push/subscribe with another user's endpoint removes that victim's subscription row and silently disables their push notifications.

findings.title: repeatMeal reads a meal by id without ownership check
findings.evidence: `db.select().from(meals).where(eq(meals.id, mealId))` (no `user_id` filter) — an authenticated attacker calls repeatMeal with another user's meal id and the meal's name, place and macros are copied into the attacker's own log, disclosing another user's data.

findings.title: updateProfileSettings spreads passthrough input into the DB update
findings.evidence: `settingsSchema` ends with `.passthrough()` (line 109) and the result is written as `.set({ ...data, updated_at: new Date() })`, so extra JSON keys sent by the client are written to the profiles row (e.g. overwriting `user_id` to hijack the profile row or setting fields such as `coach_rules`/`summary_rules` beyond their validated limits).

findings.title: Raw HTML rendered without sanitization via rehype-raw
findings.evidence: `rehypePlugins={[rehypeRaw]}` renders raw HTML embedded in markdown (coach/AI output that can be steered by user-supplied text such as meal names) with no rehype-sanitize pass, so payloads like `<iframe srcdoc="<script>…</script>">` are materialized into the DOM and executed in the app's origin.

findings.title: Cron maintenance endpoint is unauthenticated when CRON_SECRET is unset
findings.evidence: The guard is `if (cronSecret && auth !== \`Bearer ${cronSecret}\`)` — if `process.env.CRON_SECRET` is missing/empty the whole check is skipped. Any anonymous attacker can `GET /api/cron/maintenance` to repeatedly run `pruneEvents`/`expireStaleFacts`/`consolidateMemories` (destructive DB maintenance) and read the returned counts.

findings.title: rehype-raw renders unsanitized raw HTML from markdown text (stored XSS)
findings.evidence: `rehypePlugins={[rehypeRaw]}` re-enables raw HTML parsing with no `rehype-sanitize`, and the only component overrides are for safe tags. Any markdown text sourced from model output / user content (e.g. a coach reply driven by prompt injection) containing `<iframe srcdoc="<script>fetch('/api/...')</script>">` or similar is rendered as real DOM in the app origin, executing script with the victim's session.

findings.title: Unvalidated `next` query parameter passed to NextResponse.redirect
findings.evidence: `const next = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get("next"); return NextResponse.redirect(new URL(next ?? "/settings?whoop=env", request.url));` — an attacker who sends a logged-in victim to `/api/whoop/connect?next=https://evil.example/phish` (or `//evil.example`) gets a redirect off-site from the trusted domain (reachable whenever Whoop env is not configured).

findings.title: OAuth state check skipped when the state cookie is absent
findings.evidence: `if (!code || (expected && state !== expected))` — `expected` comes from `request.cookies.get("whoop_oauth_state")?.value`, so when the cookie is missing/expired the condition is false and any `state` value is accepted. An attacker can complete a Whoop OAuth flow for their own account, then lure the victim into `/api/whoop/callback?code=<attacker code>&state=x`, linking the attacker's Whoop data to the victim's account (login/account-linking CSRF).

findings.title: deleteSubscription ignores userId, allowing deletion of any user's subscription
findings.evidence: `deleteSubscription(userId, endpoint)` builds `.where(eq(push_subscriptions.endpoint, endpoint))` — the `userId` argument is never used in the filter. A logged-in attacker who supplies a victim's push endpoint to `DELETE /api/push/subscribe` deletes the victim's subscription row (denial of notifications); the sibling `deleteSubscriptionByEndpoint` shows the ownership filter was dropped by mistake.

findings.title: repeatMeal reads any user's meal by id (missing ownership check)
findings.evidence: `db.select().from(meals).where(eq(meals.id, mealId)).limit(1)` has no `eq(meals.user_id, user.id)` filter, unlike the update/delete actions. An authenticated attacker can call `repeatMeal({ mealId: <victim meal id>, category: "lunch", day: "2024-01-01" })` to copy another user's meal (name, place, macros, catalog_item_id) into their own account and read the data back.

findings.title: updateProfileSettings uses .passthrough() and spreads input into the DB update
findings.evidence: `settingsSchema` ends with `.passthrough()` and the action does `.set({ ...data, updated_at: new Date() })`, so every extra key the client sends is written to the `profiles` row (e.g. `{"sex":"male","birth_year":null,"height_cm":null,"timezone":"UTC","day_cutoff_hour":4,"user_id":"<other-id>","coach_rules":"..."}`) — arbitrary column overwrite on the profile, bypassing the field whitelist and the dedicated rules/language actions.

finding.title: OAuth state validation is skipped when the state cookie is absent
finding.evidence: `if (!code || (expected && state !== expected))` skips the state check entirely when the whoop_oauth_state cookie is missing; an attacker who obtains their own Whoop authorization code can get a logged-in victim (who never started the flow, so has no cookie) to open `/api/whoop/callback?code=ATTACKER_CODE&state=x`, force-linking the attacker's Whoop account and syncing its data into the victim's account.

finding.title: deleteSubscription ignores its userId argument, allowing cross-user deletion
finding.evidence: The DELETE filters only on `eq(push_subscriptions.endpoint, endpoint)` while the `userId` parameter is unused; any authenticated user can send `DELETE /api/push/subscribe` with `{"endpoint": "<victim's push endpoint>"}` to remove another user's subscription and silently suppress their push notifications.

finding.title: repeatMeal reads the source meal without a user ownership check
finding.evidence: `where(eq(meals.id, mealId))` has no `meals.user_id` filter (unlike updateMeal/deleteMeal in the same file); an authenticated attacker who obtains another user's mealId can call `repeatMeal` to copy that victim's meal data (name, place, macros, catalog_item_id) into the attacker's own account.

finding.title: passthrough() schema spread directly into UPDATE allows mass assignment of arbitrary profile columns

findings.title: rehype-raw with unsanitized href allows javascript: URI XSS

Markdown input containing `[click](javascript:alert(document.cookie))` will render as a clickable link that executes JavaScript when clicked.
